column1: resource§He is a resource the department will not replace easily.§他是这个部门不容易替代的**人才**。
resourceful§Resourceful is what we call people who read the manual.§我们把读了说明书的人称作**足智多谋**。
respite§There was no respite from the noise until October.§直到十月，噪音都没有**片刻停歇**。
resplendent§Resplendent in borrowed robes, he looked entirely uncomfortable.§他穿着借来的华服**光彩夺目**，却浑身不自在。
responsible§Being responsible for a decision is not the same as making it.§对一个决定**负责**，与作出这个决定不是一回事。
restitution§Restitution was ordered and never actually made.§法院判令**归还**，实际上从未执行。
restless§A restless species will not breed in a small enclosure.§**不安**定的物种在狭小围栏里不会繁殖。
restore§Restoring a photograph means deciding what to leave damaged.§**修复**一张照片，意味着决定让哪些损坏留下。
restrain§A low wall restrains the water and hides the view.§一道矮墙**拦住**了水，也挡住了视野。
restraint§The restraint on spending lasted exactly one quarter.§开支**限制**正好维持了一个季度。
restriction§Every restriction on the archive produced a workaround.§对档案馆的每一项**限制**都催生了一种变通办法。
restrictive§A restrictive clause changes the meaning; a descriptive one does not.§**限定**性从句改变意思，非限定性的则不会。
resurgence§A resurgence of the disease followed the wet summer.§多雨的夏天之后，这种疾病**重新抬头**。
resuscitation§Resuscitation was attempted for forty minutes.§**抢救**持续了四十分钟。
retain§Clay retains water; sand does not.§黏土能**保水**，沙子不能。
retentive§A retentive soil turns a good field into a bog.§**保水**的土壤会把一块好田变成沼泽。
reticence§Reticence in an interview is not the same as evasion.§访谈中的**沉默**寡言与回避不是一回事。
reticent§She is reticent in company and voluble on paper.§她在人群中**沉默**寡言，落笔却滔滔不绝。
retraction§A retraction never travels as far as the claim.§**更正**传播的范围永远不及原来的说法。
retrenchment§Retrenchment in research is paid for a decade later.§研究上的**削减**，代价要在十年后偿付。
retrieve§The dog retrieves anything except the thing you threw.§这条狗什么都**捡回来**，就是不捡你扔的那个。
retroactive§A retroactive rule change is unfair even when it improves things.§**追溯**性的规则变更即便是改善，也不公平。
retrograde§Mars appears retrograde for about ten weeks every two years.§火星每两年会有大约十周呈现**逆行**。
reveal§What the survey reveals is how little anyone measured before.§这项调查**揭示**的是从前几乎无人测量。
reverence§Reverence for a text is the enemy of reading it.§对文本的**敬畏**是阅读它的敌人。
reverential§A reverential biography tells you less than a hostile one.§一部**充满敬意**的传记告诉你的，比一部敌意的更少。
reversal§A reversal of the current happens twice a day here.§这里的水流每天两次**逆转**。
reverse§The reverse of the coin carries the date and the mint mark.§硬币**背面**刻着年份和铸币厂标记。
revise§Revise for the reader you were three years ago.§为三年前的你自己那样的读者**修改**。
revisionist§Every generation's history is the next one's revisionism.§每一代人的历史，都是下一代人的**修正主义**。
revisit§Revisit a decision only when the facts have changed.§只有在事实改变时才**重新审视**一个决定。
revitalize§A single good café revitalized the whole square.§一家好咖啡馆让整个广场**重新有了生气**。
revivalist§Revivalist architecture copies a past that never looked like that.§**复古主义**建筑模仿的是一个从未那样过的过去。
revive§An old word revived by one novelist is now everywhere.§一位小说家**复活**的一个古词，如今随处可见。
revoke§Permission once given is awkward to revoke.§许可一旦给出，**撤回**起来很尴尬。
revolutionize§Cheap glass revolutionized the household before electricity did.§在电力之前，廉价玻璃就已**彻底改变**了家庭生活。
rhapsodize§He rhapsodized for a page and said nothing about the method.§他**狂热地写**了一页，对方法只字未提。
rhetoric§Rhetoric was taught as a craft for two thousand years.§**修辞**学被当作一门手艺教了两千年。
rhetorical§A rhetorical flourish at the end undid a careful argument.§结尾一处**修辞**上的花哨毁了一个审慎的论证。
ridicule§Ridicule is the argument you use when you have none.§**嘲笑**是没有论据时使用的论证。
rigidity§Rigidity of the frame is what makes the instrument accurate.§框架的**刚性**正是这台仪器准确的原因。
rigorous§Rigorous is not the same as difficult to read.§**严谨**并不等于难读。
ritualistic§Ritualistic checking calms the mind and finds nothing.§**仪式**化的检查能安抚心神，却什么也查不出。
rival§No rival edition came close to the completeness of hers.§没有哪个**竞争**版本接近她那一版的完整度。
rivalry§Sibling rivalry produced two very different careers.§手足之间的**竞争**造就了两段截然不同的事业。
roam§His attention roamed and the argument roamed with it.§他的注意力**四处游走**，论证也跟着游走。
robust§A robust conclusion survives a change in the assumptions.§**稳健**的结论经得起假设的改变。
rouse§It takes a great deal to rouse a committee in July.§七月里要让一个委员会**振作起来**很不容易。
routine§Routine is what lets you do difficult work on a bad day.§**常规**让你在状态糟糕的日子也能做难做的事。
rudimentary§Rudimentary drainage kept the crypt dry for six centuries.§**简陋**的排水让这座地下墓室干燥了六个世纪。
ruffian§The ruffians of the ballad are farmers in the court record.§歌谣里的**恶棍**，在法庭记录里是农民。
rugged§A rugged notebook survived four field seasons.§一本**结实**的笔记本熬过了四个野外季。
rustic§Rustic simplicity is usually an expensive effect.§**乡野的质朴**通常是一种昂贵的效果。
sacrosanctity§The sacrosanctity of the reading room ended with the wifi.§阅览室的**神圣不可侵犯**，随着无线网络而告终。
sagacious§A sagacious question is worth three clever answers.§一个**睿智的**问题抵得上三个聪明的回答。
sagacity§Sagacity is experience that has been thought about.§**睿智**是经过思考的经验。
salient§Salient points are the ones a reader could repeat afterwards.§**显著的**要点，是读者事后能复述出来的那些。
salutary§A salutary reminder arrived in the form of a small fine.§一次**有益的**提醒以一小笔罚款的形式到来。
salutation§The salutation tells you how well they actually knew each other.§**称呼语**能说明他们实际上有多熟。
salvage§There was nothing to salvage from the second draft.§第二稿里没有什么可以**抢救**的。
salvageable§The negatives were salvageable; the prints were not.§底片**还能抢救**，冲印的照片则不行。
salvo§The opening salvo of the campaign was a single letter.§这场运动的**第一炮**是一封信。
sanctimonious§Nothing is more sanctimonious than a reformed smoker.§没有什么比一个戒了烟的人更**假道学**。
sanction§Sanctions were imposed, evaded, and eventually forgotten.§**制裁**被实施、被规避，最终被遗忘。
sanguine§A sanguine complexion was once read as a sign of health.§**红润**的面色曾被视为健康的标志。
sarcasm§Sarcasm is the only tone that does not survive translation.§**讽刺**是唯一在翻译中留不下来的语气。
sate§The market for the book was sated within a month.§这本书的市场需求一个月内就**饱和**了。
satirize§To satirize an institution you must first understand it.§要**讽刺**一个机构，先得理解它。
